units.text: EXT. SELF-SERVE CAR WASH - DUSK
A concrete bay, wet and humming.
Neon over the coin box.
Foam slides down a windshield.
PILAR MOSQUERA, 30s, in a rain jacket, holds a pressure wand in one hand and her phone in the other.
She is rinsing a green hatchback with great care.
No, it's fine. I'm rinsing. It's very dramatic.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: Pilar, you sound happy.
units.name: ANTON

units.text: I am happy. Is that suspicious?
units.name: PILAR

units.text: It's a little suspicious.
units.name: ANTON

units.text: She laughs.
She sprays the back bumper, then the tires.
Did you get the table?
units.name: PILAR

units.text: Seven-thirty. The one by the window.
units.name: ANTON

units.text: You remembered I like the window.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: I remember everything.
units.name: ANTON

units.text: Her smile holds a half beat too long.
She turns off the wand.
Water drips.
Anton. The window table. That's where you proposed to Rosa.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: A long silence on the line.
A distant horn.
I thought it'd be nice.
units.name: ANTON

units.text: It would be nice. For her.
units.name: PILAR

units.text: She opens the car door, slides into the driver's seat, and sets the phone on the dashboard.
Foam slides off the windshield and the world goes bright white.
I'll see you at seven-thirty.
units.name: PILAR
